Passkeys use public-key authentication tied to the website’s identity. They resist phishing better than passwords, but recovery and device synchronization depend on the provider.
The DOM is an object representation of a document. Scripts can read and modify it, causing changes to layout or behavior.
Cache-Control defines caching rules. No-cache permits storage but requires validation; no-store asks caches not to store the response. They are not interchangeable.
HTML describes the structure and semantics of a web document. Semantic elements help browsers, assistive technologies, and search systems understand content roles.
HTTP 415 means the server does not support the submitted media type or encoding for that endpoint.
WebAssembly is a compact code format designed for portable execution. In a browser it operates within sandbox and API constraints; it does not grant unrestricted system access.
A web app manifest supplies installation metadata such as name, icons, start URL, and scope. It does not itself implement offline caching.
JavaScript supplies behavior to web pages and can use browser APIs within security boundaries. It is not the same language as Java.
CSP restricts which resources a page may execute or load. It can reduce injection impact but does not replace safe rendering and input handling.
DNS translates domain names into network addresses. A DNS error can come from a typo, a local resolver, or the domain’s configuration.
sessionStorage stores per-origin data in a browsing session associated with a tab. Reloads usually preserve it; closing the tab ends the session. It is distinct from session cookies.
WebGL provides GPU-accelerated graphics through a browser-managed context. Contexts may be lost because of resource pressure, resets, or policy.

localStorage holds string key-value data for an origin and is synchronous. It can be cleared by the user and may be unavailable or restricted. It is not an appropriate place for secrets that must be hidden from site scripts.
HTTP 410 indicates that the server considers the resource no longer available, often permanently. A local cache reset is unlikely to restore it.
